ai.description: *Hemidactylus paaragowli* reaches 65 mm SVL. It is greyish-brown with dark dorsal blotches and a white venter. Distinctive features include a strongly tuberculate dorsum and a tail with whorls of spines.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hemidactylus paaragowli* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous dark stripe extending from the snout through the eye to the neck.
ai.habitat: *Hemidactylus paaragowli* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats, typically inhabiting rocky crevices and boulders within moist deciduous and evergreen forest ecosystems.
ai.behavior: The Travancore Rock Gecko is strictly nocturnal, emerging after dark to forage for small insects on vertical rock faces and trees within its specialized forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hemidactylus paaragowli* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two hard-shelled eggs. Breeding occurs throughout the year, with peak activity during the monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hemidactylus paaragowli* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, typically inhabiting rocky outcrops at elevations between 300 and 1,200 meters.
